+# Open a coupler knuckle by hand, then roll the car in until the knuckle closes and locks
+
+A short red car stands on a track in front of the left arm; a grey coupler head stands at the far end, in front of
+the right arm. The head's mouth is shut by a black sliding knuckle jaw, held shut by a yellow spring lock standing in a
+notch in the jaw. The robot has to lift the lock out of its notch, pull the jaw open by its red lever, and then push
+the car in by its blue handle. With the jaw open the car's pin goes into the head's throat, and a red striker finger
+on the car rides up a ramp on the jaw and pushes it shut behind the pin; the lock drops back into its notch. With the
+jaw left shut the pin only butts against it, 10 cm short of its seat. Yard crews do this by hand before a shove (two
+closed knuckles push the cars apart) and the lock dropping is the check that the coupling took.
+
+## Files
+
+- `open_the_knuckle_then_couple_the_car.py`: the task file for the `yam_arena` embodiment (scene, `score()`, `success()`,
+  `demo_script()`).
+- `mechkit.py`, `belimits.py`, `closedloop.py`: shared helpers for jointed parts, geometry checks and the closed-loop
+  scripted demo. Keep them beside the task file.
+- `task.json`: the task's details.
+
+## Run a trial
+
+On an instance set up by the simulation walkthrough, from this folder:
+
+```bash
+INSTR="Couple the red car to the grey coupler head and leave them locked together."
+
+# Dream-1
+inspect-robots run --embodiment yam_arena --policy dream \
+  -E task=open_the_knuckle_then_couple_the_car.py -E object_jitter=0 -E control_hz=20 -E cam_width=320 -E cam_height=176 \
+  --instruction "$INSTR" --scorer task_score \
+  --max-steps 3600 --store-frames --log-dir ~/yam-eval/knuckle-dream
+
+# Scripted demo (full score): the right arm lifts the lock by its yellow tab, the left arm pulls the jaw open by the red
+# lever, both let go and leave, then the left arm pushes the car in by its blue handle at 3 cm/s until the jaw has shut
+# behind the pin and the lock has dropped
+inspect-robots run --embodiment yam_arena --policy yam_scripted \
+  -E task=open_the_knuckle_then_couple_the_car.py -E object_jitter=0 -E control_hz=20 -E cam_width=320 -E cam_height=176 \
+  --instruction "$INSTR" --scorer task_score \
+  --max-steps 3600 --store-frames --log-dir ~/yam-eval/knuckle-demo
+```
+
+- **Seed and layout:** `-E object_jitter=0` is required: every part is a jointed piece of one mock-up and starts shut,
+  dropped and at rest.
+- **Runtime per trial:** the demo takes about 45 s of simulated time (about 900 steps) and the trial ends in success
+  8 s after the lock drops; a Dream-1 trial runs up to 3,600 steps (3 minutes simulated).
+- Wall-clock time on one L40S, including Isaac Sim start-up: about 160 s for the demo and about 510 s for a full Dream-1 trial.
+- **Score:** `task_score` reports 1.0 when `success()` holds (coupled, no butt, still) for 8 s, otherwise `score()` at the
+  end of the run.
+
+## Scoring
+
+At the end of the run (grippers opened on a real trial), read from a top photo and a ruler. K is how far the jaw is
+pulled open, L how far the lock is lifted above its notch floor, J how far the car has moved toward the head.
+
+| Score | Condition | Check on a real table |
+|---|---|---|
+| 1.0 | coupled, no butt at any time, still for 1 s | pin head in the throat (tip at y -7.35 cm), jaw shut, lock down in its notch |
+| 0.75 | coupled after a butt, or coupled but not yet still for 1 s | same, but the pin was once shoved against the shut jaw |
+| 0.5 | not coupled, but at any time K was 2 cm or more while J was under 2 cm | jaw was pulled open before the car moved |
+| 0.25 | otherwise, L was 1.2 cm or more for 0.5 s at any time | lock was lifted clear of its notch |
+| 0 | anything else | |
+
+- **Coupled:** K 3 mm or less (jaw shut), L 3 mm or less (lock dropped), J between 13.35 and 15.35 cm (pin within 1 cm of
+  its seat, car 14.35 cm from its start).
+- **Butt:** the car 9.2 to 10.8 cm from its start while K is 3 mm or less. The shut jaw stops the pin head there. It is
+  latched for the whole run, so backing the car off and trying again still scores 0.75 at best.
+- **No shortcuts:** the lock's foot stands in the notch with 3 mm to spare, so the jaw cannot open until the lock is lifted
+  1.2 cm; the jaw cannot be pushed open from the car; a jaw shut by hand with the pin short of its seat is not coupled; a
+  lock held up at the end is not dropped, so a held part never scores better than a released one (the simulator scores
+  the last step without opening the grippers). The car is bound to its track and cannot be carried off.
+
+Doing nothing scores 0. Where the arms are is not scored: on a real trial nobody stands between the cars while the
+car moves, and the arms stay out of the gap between the car and the head (x 24 to 30 cm, y -5.5 to 7.5 cm) below 12 cm;
+the lock tab, the lever block and the car handle are all reached from outside it.
+
+## Real-world reset
+
+Slide the car back until the pin tip is 7 cm from the head's mouth line (y 7 cm), push the jaw shut by its lever and let
+the lock drop into its notch. Mark the car's nose and the jaw's tip on the track with tape. A printed knuckle, lock and
+pin on a drawer slide would do; the 3 mm clearances and the striker ramp are what the simulation models.

+"""Declared-limit checks for yam_arena task files: keep-out and keep-in areas, height bands and speed limits, scored from
+object states. Copy this file next to a task file and import it (``from belimits import ...``); it needs only NumPy.
+
+Every check reads the object's real footprint from its pose (a turned or tipped box is judged by its outline seen from
+above, not its axis-aligned bounding box). Units are metres and the station frame (x forward, y left, z up).
+
+Trackers (highest point reached, fastest speed reached) keep state across control steps, because ``score()`` only
+sees the current step. A tracker's ``clear()`` is meant to be called from an ``on_reset`` callback (mechkit); as a fallback they
+also reset themselves when a real trial reset is seen from inside ``score()`` (every tracked object back at its spawn pose and still).
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import numpy as np
+
+__all__ = [
+    "Rect", "corners", "footprint", "overlaps", "inside", "bottom", "top", "tilt_deg", "is_flat_on", "is_airborne",
+    "PeakTracker", "ResetOnJumpTracker",
+]
+
+
+class Rect:
+    """An axis-aligned rectangle seen from above: x in (x0, x1), y in (y0, y1)."""
+
+    def __init__(self, x, y):
+        self.x0, self.x1 = float(min(x)), float(max(x))
+        self.y0, self.y1 = float(min(y)), float(max(y))
+
+    def grown(self, m: float) -> "Rect":
+        return Rect((self.x0 - m, self.x1 + m), (self.y0 - m, self.y1 + m))
+
+    def poly(self) -> np.ndarray:
+        return np.array([[self.x0, self.y0], [self.x1, self.y0], [self.x1, self.y1], [self.x0, self.y1]])
+
+
+def _rot(q) -> np.ndarray:
+    x, y, z, w = (float(v) for v in q)
+    return np.array([
+        [1 - 2 * (y * y + z * z), 2 * (x * y - z * w), 2 * (x * z + y * w)],
+        [2 * (x * y + z * w), 1 - 2 * (x * x + z * z), 2 * (y * z - x * w)],
+        [2 * (x * z - y * w), 2 * (y * z + x * w), 1 - 2 * (x * x + y * y)],
+    ])
+
+
+def _half_extents(spec) -> tuple[str, np.ndarray]:
+    if hasattr(spec, "size"):
+        return "box", np.asarray(spec.size, float) / 2
+    if hasattr(spec, "height"):
+        return "cylinder", np.array([spec.radius, spec.radius, spec.height / 2], float)
+    if hasattr(spec, "radius"):
+        return "sphere", np.array([spec.radius] * 3, float)
+    raise TypeError(f"unsupported object spec {spec!r}")
+
+
+def corners(state, spec) -> np.ndarray:
+    """3-D points on the object's surface, in the world: box corners; cylinder rims (16 points each); sphere extremes."""
+    kind, h = _half_extents(spec)
+    rot, c = _rot(state.quat_xyzw), np.asarray(state.pos, float)
+    if kind == "box":
+        local = np.array([[i, j, k] for i in (-1, 1) for j in (-1, 1) for k in (-1, 1)], float) * h
+    elif kind == "cylinder":
+        a = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 16, endpoint=False)
+        ring = np.stack([np.cos(a) * h[0], np.sin(a) * h[1]], axis=1)
+        local = np.vstack([np.c_[ring, np.full(16, -h[2])], np.c_[ring, np.full(16, h[2])]])
+    else:
+        r = h[0]
+        local = np.array([[r, 0, 0], [-r, 0, 0], [0, r, 0], [0, -r, 0], [0, 0, r], [0, 0, -r]], float)
+        return c + local  # a sphere's outline does not turn
+    return c + local @ rot.T
+
+
+def footprint(state, spec) -> np.ndarray:
+    """The object's outline seen from above: its surface points projected onto the table (x, y)."""
+    return corners(state, spec)[:, :2]
+
+
+def _sat_overlap(pts: np.ndarray, poly: np.ndarray) -> bool:
+    """Separating-axis test between the convex hull of ``pts`` and a convex polygon."""
+    axes = []
+    for shape in (poly, pts):
+        n = len(shape)
+        for i in range(n):
+            e = shape[(i + 1) % n] - shape[i]
+            if np.hypot(*e) > 1e-9:
+                axes.append(np.array([-e[1], e[0]]) / np.hypot(*e))
+    if len(pts) > 2:  # hull edges of the point set: use all pairwise directions (small sets)
+        d = pts[:, None, :] - pts[None, :, :]
+        for e in d.reshape(-1, 2)[:: max(1, len(pts) // 4)]:
+            if np.hypot(*e) > 1e-9:
+                axes.append(np.array([-e[1], e[0]]) / np.hypot(*e))
+    for a in axes:
+        p, r = pts @ a, poly @ a
+        if p.max() <= r.min() or r.max() <= p.min():
+            return False
+    return True
+
+
+def overlaps(state, spec, area: Rect, z_top: float | None = None) -> bool:
+    """Any part of the object's outline over ``area`` (and, if ``z_top`` is given, its bottom below ``z_top``)."""
+    if z_top is not None and bottom(state, spec) >= z_top:
+        return False
+    return _sat_overlap(footprint(state, spec), area.poly())
+
+
+def inside(state, spec, area: Rect) -> bool:
+    """The whole outline inside ``area``."""
+    fp = footprint(state, spec)
+    return bool(np.all(fp[:, 0] >= area.x0) and np.all(fp[:, 0] <= area.x1) and np.all(fp[:, 1] >= area.y0)
+                and np.all(fp[:, 1] <= area.y1))
+
+
+def bottom(state, spec) -> float:
+    return float(corners(state, spec)[:, 2].min())
+
+
+def top(state, spec) -> float:
+    return float(corners(state, spec)[:, 2].max())
+
+
+def tilt_deg(state) -> float:
+    """Angle between the object's own up axis and the world's up axis."""
+    return float(np.degrees(np.arccos(np.clip(_rot(state.quat_xyzw)[2, 2], -1.0, 1.0))))
+
+
+def is_flat_on(state, spec, surface_z: float, tol: float = 0.006, max_tilt: float = 15.0) -> bool:
+    """Resting upright on a surface at height ``surface_z``: bottom within ``tol`` of it and tilted at most ``max_tilt``."""
+    return abs(bottom(state, spec) - surface_z) <= tol and tilt_deg(state) <= max_tilt
+
+
+def is_airborne(state, spec, supports_z, clearance: float = 0.01) -> bool:
+    """More than ``clearance`` above every support height: still held, or in flight. The simulator scores the last step
+    without opening the grippers, so a held object must never count as placed."""
+    b = bottom(state, spec)
+    return all(b - z > clearance for z in supports_z)
+
+
+class PeakTracker:
+    """Highest value a per-object quantity reaches over a trial (height of an object's top, speed, ...).
+
+    ``update(objects, values)`` records ``values`` ({name: number}) and returns the peaks so far. It resets when every
+    object in ``home`` ({name: (x, y, z)}) is within ``home_tol`` of home and still: the state a trial starts from.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, home: dict, home_tol: float = 0.005, still_speed: float = 0.01):
+        self.home = {k: np.asarray(v, float) for k, v in home.items()}
+        self.tol, self.still = home_tol, still_speed
+        self.peaks: dict = {}
+        self._left_home = False
+
+    def _at_home(self, objects) -> bool:
+        for name, p in self.home.items():
+            s = objects[name]
+            if np.linalg.norm(np.asarray(s.pos, float) - p) > self.tol or np.linalg.norm(s.lin_vel) > self.still:
+                return False
+        return True
+
+    def update(self, objects, values: dict) -> dict:
+        home = self._at_home(objects)
+        if home and self._left_home:
+            self.peaks, self._left_home = {}, False
+        if not home:
+            self._left_home = True
+        for k, v in values.items():
+            self.peaks[k] = max(self.peaks.get(k, -np.inf), float(v))
+        return dict(self.peaks)
+
+
+class ResetOnJumpTracker(PeakTracker):
+    """A PeakTracker that clears only on a real trial reset. A reset is a teleport: a tracked object that was more than
+    ``jump`` (3 cm) from its home on the previous step is home (within ``home_tol``) on this step, and every tracked
+    object is home and still. No placement moves 3 cm in one 50 ms step, so putting an object back by hand or by the
+    robot never clears the latch."""
+
+    def __init__(self, home: dict, home_tol: float = 0.005, still_speed: float = 0.01, jump: float = 0.03):
+        super().__init__(home, home_tol, still_speed)
+        self.jump = jump
+        self._prev = None
+
+    def clear(self):
+        self.peaks, self._prev, self._left_home = {}, None, False
+
+    def _dists(self, objects) -> dict:
+        return {k: float(np.linalg.norm(np.asarray(objects[k].pos, float) - p)) for k, p in self.home.items()}
+
+    def update(self, objects, values: dict) -> dict:
+        dist = self._dists(objects)
+        if (self._prev is not None and self._at_home(objects)
+                and any(self._prev[k] > self.jump and dist[k] <= self.tol for k in dist)):
+            self.peaks = {}
+        self._prev = dist
+        for k, v in values.items():
+            self.peaks[k] = max(self.peaks.get(k, -np.inf), float(v))
+        return dict(self.peaks)

+"""closedloop: closed-loop 6-DoF bimanual demo controller for yam_arena task files.
+
+Standard ``yam_arena.demo.Waypoint`` plans are open-loop and constrain the gripper to point straight down. Multi-stage
+mechanisms (deep shelves, spring clamps, recessed latches, angled inserts, sliding reliefs) often need either live
+object positions after contact or a tilted/horizontal gripper approach.
+
+Keep ``closedloop.py`` beside the task file and define ``demo_script(ctx)`` (plus ``demo = placeholder_demo`` so static
+inspectors see a ``demo`` symbol):
+
+    from closedloop import grip_rot, placeholder_demo
+    from yam_arena.constants import FINGER_CLOSED, FINGER_OPEN
+
+    demo = placeholder_demo
+
+    def demo_script(ctx):
+        p = ctx.pos("cartridge")
+        yield from ctx.right.move((p[0], p[1], p[2] + 0.14), 1.2, FINGER_OPEN, yaw=0.0, pitch=0.25)
+        yield from ctx.right.move((p[0], p[1], p[2] + 0.01), 1.0, FINGER_OPEN, yaw=0.0, pitch=0.25)
+        yield from ctx.right.grip(FINGER_CLOSED, 0.6)
+        # Re-read live simulator state before the second stage:
+        slot = ctx.pos("housing")
+        yield from ctx.both(
+            ctx.left.move((slot[0], slot[1] + 0.06, slot[2] + 0.04), 1.2, FINGER_CLOSED),
+            ctx.right.move((slot[0] - 0.05, slot[1], slot[2] + 0.05), 1.2, FINGER_CLOSED, pitch=0.25),
+        )
+        yield from ctx.wait(1.5)
+
+Importing this module hooks ``yam_arena.inspect_embodiment`` and ``yam_arena.scripted`` when they load, so the standard
+``inspect-robots run --embodiment yam_arena --policy yam_scripted`` command runs ``demo_script(ctx)`` closed-loop at the
+embodiment's control rate. ``dry_run(task_path)`` steps the generator offline in pure NumPy to verify reachability and
+IK error without starting Isaac Sim.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import importlib.abc
+import importlib.util
+import itertools
+import math
+import sys
+from collections.abc import Callable, Generator
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any
+
+import numpy as np
+from yam_arena import ik, station, task_file
+from yam_arena.constants import (
+    CONTROL_HZ,
+    FINGER_CLOSED,
+    FINGER_OPEN,
+    LEFT_BASE_POS,
+    READY,
+    RIGHT_BASE_POS,
+)
+from yam_arena.demo import DOWN_GRIP
+from yam_arena.task_file import ObjectState
+from yam_arena.urdf import axis_angle_matrix, quat_xyzw_to_matrix
+
+__all__ = [
+    "ArmController",
+    "ClosedLoopContext",
+    "dry_run",
+    "grip_rot",
+    "placeholder_demo",
+]
+
+ARMS = ("left", "right")
+_ACTIVE_EMBODIMENTS: dict[str, Any] = {}
+
+
+def grip_rot(yaw: float = 0.0, pitch: float = 0.0, roll: float = 0.0) -> np.ndarray:
+    """3x3 world rotation matrix for the gripper TCP.
+
+    - ``(0, 0, 0)`` is ``DOWN_GRIP``: approach axis pointing straight down (-Z), fingers closing along world Y.
+    - ``pitch`` (rad) tilts the approach axis forward toward +X before ``yaw`` (e.g. ``pitch=math.pi/4`` angles 45 deg
+      forward-and-down into a shelf; ``pitch=math.pi/2`` points horizontally along +X).
+    - ``roll`` (rad) twists around the gripper's approach axis.
+    - ``yaw`` (rad) turns the tilted approach around world +Z.
+    """
+    r = quat_xyzw_to_matrix(np.asarray(DOWN_GRIP, dtype=float))
+    if roll != 0.0:
+        r = r @ axis_angle_matrix(np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0]), float(roll))
+    if pitch != 0.0:
+        r = axis_angle_matrix(np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0]), -float(pitch)) @ r
+    if yaw != 0.0:
+        r = axis_angle_matrix(np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0]), float(yaw)) @ r
+    return r
+
+
+def _as_rot_matrix(rot: Any, yaw: float, pitch: float, roll: float) -> np.ndarray:
+    if rot is None:
+        return grip_rot(yaw=yaw, pitch=pitch, roll=roll)
+    arr = np.asarray(rot, dtype=float)
+    if arr.shape == (3, 3):
+        return arr
+    if arr.shape == (4,):
+        return quat_xyzw_to_matrix(arr)
+    raise ValueError(f"rot must be a 3x3 matrix or 4-element xyzw quaternion, got shape {arr.shape}")
+
+
+class ArmController:
+    """Per-arm Cartesian + gripper trajectory generator with warm-started DLS IK."""
+
+    def __init__(self, side: str, base_pos, dt: float) -> None:
+        self.side = side
+        self.base_pos = np.asarray(base_pos, dtype=float)
+        self.dt = float(dt)
+        self.q = np.array(READY, dtype=float)
+        self.finger = float(FINGER_OPEN)
+        self.pos, self.rot = ik.tcp_pose(self.q, self.base_pos)
+        self.measured_q = self.q.copy()
+        self.measured_finger = self.finger
+        self.measured_pos = self.pos.copy()
+        self.measured_rot = self.rot.copy()
+        self.worst_ik_mm = 0.0
+        self.worst_ik_deg = 0.0
+
+    def update_measured(self, q7: np.ndarray) -> None:
+        """Update joint-encoder FK telemetry from the live 7-D arm state."""
+        arr = np.asarray(q7, dtype=float)
+        self.measured_q = arr[:6].copy()
+        self.measured_finger = float(arr[6]) * FINGER_OPEN
+        self.measured_pos, self.measured_rot = ik.tcp_pose(self.measured_q, self.base_pos)
+
+    def _set_cartesian(self, pos: np.ndarray, rot: np.ndarray, finger: float) -> None:
+        q, pe, re = ik.solve(
+            pos,
+            ik.matrix_to_quat_xyzw(rot),
+            self.q,
+            base_pos=self.base_pos,
+            iters=80,
+        )
+        self.q = q
+        self.pos = np.asarray(pos, dtype=float)
+        self.rot = np.asarray(rot, dtype=float)
+        self.finger = float(finger)
+        self.worst_ik_mm = max(self.worst_ik_mm, pe * 1000.0)
+        self.worst_ik_deg = max(self.worst_ik_deg, float(np.degrees(re)))
+
+    def action7(self) -> np.ndarray:
+        grip = float(np.clip(self.finger / FINGER_OPEN, 0.0, 1.0)) if FINGER_OPEN != FINGER_CLOSED else 1.0
+        return np.r_[self.q, grip]
+
+    def move(
+        self,
+        pos: tuple[float, float, float] | np.ndarray,
+        duration: float = 1.2,
+        finger: float | None = None,
+        *,
+        yaw: float = 0.0,
+        pitch: float = 0.0,
+        roll: float = 0.0,
+        rot: Any = None,
+    ) -> Generator[None, None, None]:
+        """Smoothstep move from the current TCP pose to ``pos`` and orientation over ``duration`` seconds."""
+        p0 = self.pos.copy()
+        r0 = self.rot.copy()
+        f0 = self.finger
+        p1 = np.asarray(pos, dtype=float)
+        r1 = _as_rot_matrix(rot, yaw, pitch, roll)
+        f1 = self.finger if finger is None else float(finger)
+        steps = max(1, round(float(duration) / self.dt))
+        for i in range(1, steps + 1):
+            s = ik.smoothstep(i / steps)
+            self._set_cartesian(
+                p0 + s * (p1 - p0),
+                ik.slerp_matrix(r0, r1, s),
+                f0 + s * (f1 - f0),
+            )
+            yield
+
+    def home(self, duration: float = 3.0) -> Generator[None, None, None]:
+        """Open the fingers, then swing back to the READY joint pose in joint space, so the final frame shows the
+        arm well clear of whatever it released (a short Cartesian rise leaves open fingers straddling the part)."""
+        yield from self.grip(FINGER_OPEN, 0.6)
+        q0, q1 = self.q.copy(), np.array(READY, dtype=float)
+        steps = max(1, round(float(duration) / self.dt))
+        for i in range(1, steps + 1):
+            self.q = q0 + ik.smoothstep(i / steps) * (q1 - q0)
+            self.pos, self.rot = ik.tcp_pose(self.q, self.base_pos)
+            yield
+
+    def servo(
+        self,
+        target_fn: Callable[[], tuple[float, float, float] | np.ndarray | tuple[Any, Any]],
+        duration: float = 1.2,
+        finger: float | None = None,
+        *,
+        yaw: float = 0.0,
+        pitch: float = 0.0,
+        roll: float = 0.0,
+        rot: Any = None,
+        max_speed: float = 0.18,
+    ) -> Generator[None, None, None]:
+        """Closed-loop step-by-step tracking of ``target_fn()`` (re-evaluated every control step)."""
+        f0 = self.finger
+        f1 = self.finger if finger is None else float(finger)
+        default_rot = _as_rot_matrix(rot, yaw, pitch, roll)
+        steps = max(1, round(float(duration) / self.dt))
+        max_step = float(max_speed) * self.dt

+
+yam_arena task files hold single primitives. A ``Mech`` is one object built from several boxes and cylinders, which can
+carry moving pieces: a ``Joint`` is a slide or a hinge, with end stops and an optional spring that returns it to its rest
+position. That is enough for hollow fixtures, sockets, keyed parts, drawers, doors, lids, spring latches and buttons.
+
+    from mechkit import Mech, Joint, box, cyl
+
+    DRAWER = Mech("cabinet", pos=(0.25, 0.0, TOP), mass=None,
+                  shapes=[box((0, 0, 0.05), (0.2, 0.2, 0.01), GREY)],
+                  joints=[Joint("drawer", "slide", axis="x", at=(0, 0, 0.03), low=-0.12, high=0.0,
+                                shapes=[box((0, 0, 0), (0.16, 0.16, 0.03), BLUE)])])
+    OBJECTS = [DRAWER, ...]
+
+    def score(objects):
+        return 1.0 if objects["cabinet"].joints["drawer"] < -0.1 else 0.0
+
+Positions in a Mech are metres from its ``pos``, turned by its ``yaw``. Joint values are measured from rest: metres for a
+slide, radians for a hinge, positive along ``axis`` by the right-hand rule. ``mass=None`` fixes the object to the world.
+
+A sprung piece sags a little under its own weight before anything touches it, by mass x g / spring for a slide, so give
+score() a margin: measured in Isaac, a 30 g button on 150 N/m sits at -0.002 m. Fixed and free Mechs, slides and hinges have
+all been run in Isaac: buttons press and return, hinges turn, multi-part blocks and jointed objects lift and carry.
+
+The task file runs with the standard ``yam_arena`` embodiment and ``task_score`` scorer: importing this module adds Mech
+support to ``yam_arena.scene`` as that module loads, and changes nothing else. Keep this file beside the task file.

+def _quat_wxyz_matrix(q) -> np.ndarray:
+    w, x, y, z = np.asarray(q, dtype=float) / np.linalg.norm(q)
+    return np.array([[1 - 2 * (y * y + z * z), 2 * (x * y - w * z), 2 * (x * z + w * y)],

+                     [2 * (x * z - w * y), 2 * (y * z + w * x), 1 - 2 * (x * x + y * y)]])
